Reference implementation (Python 3.12+):
```python
def has_negative_cycle(n, edges):
    # Initializing every distance to zero acts like a zero-cost super-source,
    # so this detects a negative cycle in any component.
    dist=[0]*n
    for iteration in range(n):
        changed=False
        for u,v,w in edges:
            if dist[v] > dist[u] + w:
                dist[v] = dist[u] + w; changed=True
        if not changed: return False
    return True

assert has_negative_cycle(3, [(0,1,1),(1,2,-3),(2,0,1)])
assert not has_negative_cycle(3, [(0,1,2),(1,2,1)])
```
explanation: Bellman–Ford relaxes every edge up to V times. Initializing all distances to zero models a super-source and can detect a negative cycle anywhere; O(VE) time.
